objectives.wording: Connect landmark discoveries to modern practice and distinguish beneficial microbial roles from disease.
Compare bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites by structure, growth, classification and representative infections.
Explain genetic targets and compare molecular diagnostic methods by the questions they answer.
Choose microscopy, culture, antigen detection or molecular testing for representative infections.
Choose a microbiological test in a simulated case and interpret the report in clinical context.
Select specimens, patient instructions, collection timing and transport conditions for representative tests.
Demonstrate patient instruction, collection, labelling and transport in simulation.
Demonstrate respectful and traceable handling of a simulated patient specimen.
Role-play collection instructions and pretest and post-test discussions with patients, relatives and clinicians.
Demonstrate secure handling and communication of an identifiable laboratory result.
Perform Gram staining on approved teaching material and report the findings.
Perform Ziehl-Neelsen staining on approved teaching material and report the findings.
Perform routine stool examination on approved teaching material.
Identify representative causative agents on supplied stool microscopy and report distinguishing features.
Use transmission patterns and population data to explain a representative outbreak and its control.
Compare the mechanisms, applications and quality controls of physical and chemical methods of sterilisation.
Compare the mechanisms and applications of disinfectants and antiseptics.
Select a method for representative laboratory, clinical and surgical scenarios and justify it.
Compare barriers and immune responses in health and disease.
Map the organs and cells of the immune system and their roles.
Explain how antigens, antibodies and complement interact, including complement activation pathways.
Explain antibody-mediated effector mechanisms during representative infections.
Explain cell-mediated effector mechanisms during representative infections.
Compare host defences against bacterial, mycobacterial, viral, fungal and parasitic infections.
Explain how representative assays detect host responses and how timing affects interpretation.
Compare active and passive immunisation and their uses.
Explain how population immunity affects transmission.
Compare types of hypersensitivity and select representative laboratory investigations.
Explain autoimmunity and select representative laboratory investigations.
Compare primary and secondary immunodeficiencies and select representative laboratory investigations.
Explain graft recognition and its implications for transplant management.
Explain tumour surveillance and immune escape and their implications for management.
Trace poststreptococcal injury and relate presentation, sequelae and laboratory evidence.
Classify representative cases and relate organisms and host factors to pathogenesis and presentation.
Interpret representative microscopy, serology and cultures in suspected cases.
Explain blood culture collection and processing and integrate microbiology with other diagnostic findings in suspected endocarditis or sepsis.
Define pyrexia of unknown origin and describe its types. Discuss the aetiopathogenesis of infectious causes and the diagnostic methods used to rule them out.
Compare causative organisms and trace pathogenesis, clinical evolution, complications, diagnosis and prevention.
Select tests by illness duration and distinguish investigation of suspected carriage.
Interpret representative culture and serology results and explain limitations.
Classify infectious causes of anaemia by mechanism: blood loss, haemolysis and impaired production.
Compare morphology, life cycles, injury, diagnosis and prevention of representative parasites.
Compare malaria parasites by morphology, life cycle, presentation, tests and prevention.
Use representative smear findings to distinguish falciparum from other malaria species and explain the limits of serology in acute diagnosis.
Describe the morphology, life cycle, presentation, diagnosis and prevention of visceral leishmaniasis.
Describe the morphology, life cycle, presentation, diagnosis and prevention of lymphatic filariasis.
Trace transmission and disease progression and explain opportunistic infections, diagnosis, prevention and management principles.
Distinguish infectious diarrhoea from dysentery and food poisoning and match representative organisms to each.
Compare representative agents by epidemiology, morphology, mechanisms, presentation and diagnostic tests.
Compare representative agents by epidemiology, morphology, mechanisms, presentation and diagnostic tests.
Compare major microbial causes and distinguish toxin-mediated illness from infection using timing and laboratory findings.
Relate Helicobacter pylori to acid peptic disease and compare diagnostic and eradication principles.
Describe the epidemiology, aetiopathogenesis, clinical features and complications of viral hepatitis.
Compare viral markers and prevention strategies by hepatitis virus.
Select and interpret markers in representative cases to distinguish infection type and phase.
Relate representative organisms to predisposing conditions, clinical course and suitable specimen handling and tests.
Compare representative microbial causes of osteomyelitis and select tests by mechanism.
Compare representative microbial causes of septic arthritis and select tests by mechanism.
Compare representative microbial causes by depth, clinical course and diagnostic approach.
Differentiate infectious and noninfectious lesions and recognize representative systemic infections with cutaneous findings.
Compare the presentations and complications of leprosy and select appropriate sampling and laboratory tests.
Compare representative presentations of cutaneous tuberculosis and atypical mycobacterial skin infection and select laboratory tests.
Compare representative bacterial, viral, fungal and parasitic causes by pathogenesis, course and diagnostic workup.
Interpret supplied Gram stains, CSF findings and cultures alongside other tests to distinguish likely causes.
Compare representative microbial causes by exposure, pathogenesis, clinical course and diagnostic workup.
Compare representative microbial causes, diagnostic approaches and prevention.
Interpret supplied Gram or Albert-stained throat smears and correlate findings with the clinical scenario.
Compare bacterial, mycobacterial, viral, fungal and parasitic causes and select tests and prevention measures.
Interpret supplied Gram and acid-fast stains from lower respiratory samples and correlate findings with clinical data.
Predict likely pathogens by age, immune status and community or healthcare setting.
Compare representative bacterial, viral, fungal and parasitic causes and select appropriate specimens and tests.
Compare representative bacterial and viral STIs by pathogenesis, diagnostic testing and prevention.
Distinguish representative UTI settings, explain mechanisms and choose collection and diagnostic methods.
Classify representative zoonoses and map reservoirs, vectors or transmission routes, illness, diagnosis and prevention.
Link host risk factors to representative opportunistic agents and select suitable laboratory investigations.
Explain representative microbial and viral oncogenic mechanisms and link preventable exposures to prevention measures.
Compare drivers of emergence and re-emergence and propose surveillance and control measures for a scenario.
Match representative Indian infection programmes and reference centres to their prevention and diagnostic roles using current programme documents.
Define healthcare-associated infection and relate common agents and infection types to breaks in transmission.
Compare standard and transmission-based precautions and explain the role of the infection control committee.
Demonstrate hand hygiene in simulation.
Demonstrate donning and doffing of personal protective equipment in simulation.
Demonstrate biomedical waste segregation in simulation.
Explain sampling and interpretation for microbial contamination of food, water and hospital air.
Link selection and transmission of resistant pathogens to representative healthcare infections and control measures.
Compare genetic and phenotypic mechanisms of antimicrobial resistance.
Distinguish intrinsic from acquired resistance and relate antimicrobial spectrum to representative organisms.
Interpret a representative antimicrobial susceptibility report.
Explain stewardship and justify a simulated prescribing decision using microbiology, review and de-escalation principles.
